title: AI handwriting analysis shows two scribes wrote the Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaa)
summary: AI handwriting analysis showed two scribes wrote the Great Isaiah Scroll, switching at columns 27–29; published in PLOS ONE 21 April 2021
account: On 21 April 2021 Mladen Popović, Maruf Dhali and Lambert Schomaker of the University of Groningen published in PLOS ONE an artificial-intelligence analysis of the handwriting of the Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaa) from the Dead Sea Scrolls. Using pattern recognition on digitized images of the scroll's 54 columns, they found that the columns fall into two statistically distinct groups, with a transition in columns 27–29, and concluded that two main scribes with different writing patterns were responsible for the scroll, against the view that one scribe wrote it. Some earlier scholars had suggested a change after column 27 on other grounds; the AI analysis supplied quantitative evidence. The team is both developer of the method and author of the finding; acceptance rests on the journal's peer review.
purpose: Writer identification in ancient manuscripts to distinguish individual scribes
